summary: Checked the item's first step (Vieta-type automorphisms of the ES surface). The ES surface F = 4xyz - n(xy+yz+zx) = x(4yz - n(y+z)) - n*yz is linear in each variable, so each (y,z)-fibre has at most one x and no Markoff-type second root exists; the repo already records this (toric model with one point per side, 'no involutions', only S3 visible). Also contrasts MARKOFF_ES.md's S_{n,D}, which has fibrewise Pell orbits only.
evidence: GEOMETRY_ES.md §2.2 (toric model, 'no involutions'), GEOMETRY_ES.md table §6 row 'Markoff-type' (line ~403)

summary: Not actionable: 1/R = 1/x+1/y+1/z with R = n/4 is literally the ES equation, a restatement with no new test. Literature check (Eppstein's Egyptian fractions & parallel resistors page) shows only the classical pedagogical identification of unit-fraction sums with parallel resistors; no three-branch realizability result beyond ES itself.

Checked the natural Belyi candidates: the Fermat curve of exponent p is a (p,p,p) cover with chi = 3/p - 1 (not 4/p - 1); X(p)/X_0(p) have cusps (2,3,inf)-type. Every ES triple has x,y,z > p/4, so for p > 4*M0 (M0 = largest entry in Takeuchi's finite list of arithmetic triangle groups, Tak77 Thm 3; exact M0 not checked) no ES triangle group is arithmetic, and no finite-index subgroup can be a congruence/Shimura-curve uniformisation: the modular-Belyi route is closed for large p. Dessins with ES passport are not thereby excluded (Assessment).
evidence: Calegari arXiv:2501.01780 §1.1 (76 cocompact arithmetic triangle groups, citing Takeuchi 1977 Thm 3)

Computed the exact ES counts f(p) = #{x<=y<=z : 1/x+1/y+1/z = 4/p} for all 1437 primes p <= 11987 (exact integer re-verification). Mean f(p) rises from 28.8 (p in [100,200)) to 122.7 ([6400,12800)); mean/log^2 p rises 1.17 -> 1.48 and mean/log^3 p falls 0.24 -> 0.16, local exponent in ln(log p) is ~2.4 (noisy), so neither pure log^2 nor pure log^3 fits. The repo has both (B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md line 87 says log^2, z31_unit_fractions.md §(c) says log^3); the expected-count comparison itself is already recorded there. Recommend reconciling the exponent claims.

Read Liu-Sawhney arXiv:2404.07113 'On further questions regarding unit fractions' (full text, 22 pp.) for bounded-length results with dense denominators. Found none: Thm 1.1 (log-density, unboundedly many terms), Prop 1.4 (dense A gives B with sum s/t, t <= exp(C/alpha), term count unbounded), Thms 1.5/1.6 (Yokota-type, unbounded term counts). Erdos-Graham Problems 305/310 are also about unbounded term counts, so a bounded-k dense-denominator statement is not in the literature I could read.

summary: Not actionable as stated: the first step is 'low priority' with no concrete test, and phi(n) | n-1 gives no Egyptian-fraction constraint on 4/p = sum of three unit fractions, so there is no ES content to test. Recorded only as a sibling problem.

Formal triviality with no ES content: ES(n) is already Sigma_1 by its own definition (exists x,y,z >= 1 with 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx)), so it is Diophantine; a positive-valued polynomial for the set is a standard consequence of MRDP/Jones and adds no arithmetic information. Not a route to a proof; logic framing is already in logic_complexity.
